title: Blind Tone singing the Titanic ballad
summary: Blind singers performed at the pay office; Barker describes Blind Tone's guitar blues and his ballad of the Titanic.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Did the blind men have any answer too much to it?

Guitar shit, naturally. I remember one was called Blind Tone. It was sensational. First time I actually saw somebody who was really singing the blues, it was well known. Everybody was so happy they'd come from blocks around. The news was spreading inside of fifteen to twenty minutes of that, two, three hundred people gathered around. The first time I saw somebody, I had the nuts through the crowd to see if it was exciting. Sitting down on a box or a crate with this old blind man. Didn't seem to be so old, maybe in his fifties, playing these blues on the guitar thing. And he sang the ballad of the Titanic. He sang this thing, of course it was some connection with the riverfront, all the men know about boats, the loaded boats. That was his main concept. He sang the city. Great ballad. He'd sing all about the Titanic, all the millionaires on the boat. And the island was crying and screaming. He didn't want to go down with the ship. Of course they had to go down. Hit that big iceberg. He described the iceberg in detail. He described Vanderbilt when he was piloting out of the boat and leaving my maids behind. And all these women going down in the ocean and the salt of the sea to waste. And the sharks were going to eat them up. He'd tell them to dramatize this drastic stir. But how the captain's staff stood at the wheel and went down with his ship. And he'd go on to do this thing for about twenty minutes. It was about a time ten. The captain went off his coast. Every morning he'd do that to give him. He gave him more as he did. He was up in the cabin drinking some fine whiskey. And the ship went off his coast and hit this ice boat. And it was the captain's father.
